points.text: Human performance undefined; no inter-annotator ceiling or between-annotator variance reported.
Agreement statistics (kappa, ARI, rho, tau) compared across tasks though not commensurable.
Low agreement treated as dataset defect though it may reflect valid subjectivity.
Annotator consent, compensation, welfare and ethics statement missing.
All-male narrow annotator panel not discussed as limitation of 'human performance'.
Recommendations for model developers premature given single-annotator non-English pairs.
Human and model protocols not matched despite claim; model-side protocol undocumented.
No confidence intervals or significance tests on tiny samples; ranking claims unsupported.
Aggregation of annotators into one human score undefined; some numbers inconsistent with averaging.
All non-English results from one annotator; idiosyncrasy and cultural knowledge inseparable.
Headline score pools different metrics and is mostly English.
Category averages are English-only but presented as overall averages.
Claim that models exploit patterns where humans disagree never tested; counter-cases exist.
Reported numbers contradict each other (Emotion best model, appendix agreement values).
High/low agreement thresholds applied inconsistently across tasks.
STS22-Russian recommended for replacement despite no agreement measured.
Guidelines text, sampling procedure, source split, annotator time and pay not given.
Caption counts and values inconsistent (5 vs 4 pairs, 58.7 vs 58.5, 16 tasks).
Related work omits assessor disagreement, superhuman-claim critiques and label-noise literature.
STS22-Russian replacement unsupported: no agreement measured, generic example.
Russian sentiment described as ambiguous yet high human score and cultural-gap evidence.
Models reproducing ArXiv submitter labels is not by itself a dataset flaw.
Model pool narrow, lacks strong multilingual models; rank claims depend on it.
Cultural-knowledge explanation for non-English human advantage asserted without test.
'Generalizable framework' is thin; no procedure or new task demonstrated.
MTEB variants' human validation and Emotion label provenance not described.
Human and model protocols unmatched and model-side protocol undocumented.
Causal claim that models exploit patterns untested; alternatives ignored.
Low agreement on 30-48 items without intervals used to condemn datasets.
Agreement thresholds applied inconsistently (Toxicity, STSBenchmark).
ARI on free-cluster annotations sensitive to number of clusters chosen.
Cultural-knowledge explanation rests on one annotator, English-only models, ambiguous dataset.
Headline score pools four metrics and is mostly English.
Headline lacks interval; humans ranked 4th among models separated by tiny margins.
Wording overclaims: generalization, fundamental unreliability, replacement, few samples, state-of-the-art.
'5 of 14' caption vs 4 pairs where humans top.
Emotion best-model 87.1 vs 75.4 inconsistency.
Agreement values differ between appendix sections.
STS22-Russian pattern illustrated by generic, unverifiable example.
Category averages English-only without saying so.
Conclusions (quality issues, replacement, few samples, pattern exploitation) overstated.
Counts and labels inconsistent across captions; averages coverage unclear.
Headline hides uncertainty; '4th place' implies false precision.
Headline average mixes different metrics.
'Generalizable framework' claim unsupported with four task types, five languages.
Appendix long and carries statistics differing from main text.
Captions use '%' for Spearman correlations.
Motivation for human performance evaluation unconvincing.
Retrieval task not included in human evaluation.
Most tasks have only two annotators; reliability concern.
Only 20-50 instances annotated per task.
Comparing native low-resource speakers with English-trained models is unfair.
Only one or two annotators; results may reflect individual bias.
30-50 items per dataset too few; low statistical power.
No analysis of underlying causes such as training data or cultural mismatch.
No experiment with LLMs following the same annotation protocol.
Retrieval tasks omitted.
Unclear whether human instructions align with original dataset annotation schemes.
Small, homogeneous all-male annotator pool, single annotators for some languages.
Evaluation sets are small.
No confidence intervals reported.
Attributing superhuman model results to data quality issues is not rigorous.
Retrieval not included.
Agreement-weighted evaluation idea underdeveloped.
Only 20-50 instances per task; reliability of conclusions doubtful.
Only four task types covered; retrieval missing.
No significance testing for comparisons.

P.summary: Human score definition/aggregation unclear; no inter-annotator ceiling.
Agreement statistics incommensurable across task types.
Disagreement and label reproduction wrongly read as dataset defects.
Annotator ethics, consent and compensation missing.
Homogeneous annotator panel not discussed as limitation.
Developer recommendations premature.
Human and model protocols unmatched and undocumented.
No uncertainty estimates or significance tests; rank claims unsupported.
Non-English results single-annotator; cultural-knowledge explanation untested.
Headline average pools different metrics, mostly English.
Category averages English-only.
Pattern-exploitation causal claim untested.
Inconsistent statistics across text, tables and appendix.
Agreement thresholds applied inconsistently.
STS22-Russian replacement recommendation unsupported.
Human-side reproducibility details missing.
Caption counts inconsistent.
Related work on assessor agreement, superhuman critiques, label noise missing.
Russian sentiment narrative inconsistent.
Narrow model pool lacking strong multilingual models.
Framework claim thin and overgeneralized.
MTEB variants and Emotion label provenance undescribed.
Conclusions and wording overclaim relative to evidence.
Percent sign used for Spearman correlations.

Q.summary: Too few annotated instances per task.
No confidence intervals or significance testing.
Unfair comparison of native speakers with English-trained models.
Causes of human-model differences not analysed rigorously.
Human instructions alignment with original annotation unclear.
